titel: Fruit sinks to the bottom of the cake
kurz: Fruit sinks when the batter cannot hold it up or the fruit is heavy and wet: it drops before the batter sets.
bild_im_kopf: Like stones in honey and in water: in thick honey they stay suspended, in water they drop straight to the bottom.
faustregeln: For evenly spread [[w-obst|fruit]]: thick batter, small dry pieces.
Fold frozen berries in still frozen, don't thaw them first.

ursachen.warum: A thin batter offers too little support. In the oven it first gets even runnier before it sets.
fix: Use a thicker batter that drops heavily from the spoon
Pour in some batter without fruit first, scatter the fruit on top

ursachen.titel: Fruit too large, wet or frozen
ursachen.warum: Large, heavy pieces sink faster. Wet fruit makes the batter around it runny.
fix: Pat the fruit dry and cut it smaller
Toss in a little flour: it helps a bit, a thicker batter helps more

ursachen.titel: The cake takes a long time to set
ursachen.warum: A large tin or an oven that is too cool gives the fruit more time to sink.
fix: Preheat the oven properly and check its temperature

q1.frage: Was the batter thick and did it drop heavily from the spoon?

q2.frage: Was the fruit large, wet or frozen?
